message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about BMI (Body Mass Index) standards used worldwide.

## What is BMI?

BMI is a screening measure that estimates body fat using a person's weight relative to their height. It is calculated as:
- **Formula**: weight (kg) ÷ [height (m)]²
- **US units**: (weight in pounds × 703) ÷ (height in inches)²

---

## Standard BMI Classification (WHO/NIH - for White, Hispanic, and Black adults)

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal/Healthy Weight | 18.5 to 24.9 |
| Overweight | 25.0 to 29.9 |
| Obesity Class I | 30.0 to 34.9 |
| Obesity Class II | 35.0 to 39.9 |
| Obesity Class III (Severe Obesity) | 40.0 or greater |

This classification has been adopted by the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** and **World Health Organization (WHO)** and is widely used in the United States and many other countries.

---

## Asian-Specific BMI Standards

Research has shown that Asian populations experience higher metabolic risks at lower BMI values. Therefore, adjusted cutoffs apply:

| Category | Asian BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|------------------------|
| Underweight | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal | 18.5 to 22.9 |
| Overweight | 23.0 to 24.9 |
| Obesity | 25.0 or greater |

Some Asian guidelines (such as Singapore's) use:
- **Healthy range**: 18.5 to 22.9 kg/m²
- **Overweight**: ≥23.0 kg/m²
- **Obese**: ≥27.5 kg/m²

---

## China's Adult BMI Standards (WS/T 428-2013)

| Category | BMI Range (kg/m²) |
|----------|-------------------|
| Underweight (体重过低) | Less than 18.5 |
| Normal (体重正常) | 18.5 to 23.9 |
| Overweight (超重) | 24.0 to 27.9 |
| Obese (肥胖) | 28.0 or greater |

---

## Special Populations

### Elderly Adults
- **General elderly recommendation**: BMI 20.0–26.9 kg/m² (China Dietary Guidelines)
- **Ages 80+**: BMI 22.0–26.9 kg/m² recommended (Chinese Nutrition Society guidelines)
- Some international sources suggest 23.0–28.0 for seniors

### Children and Teens
- BMI is calculated the same way but interpreted using **age and sex-specific percentiles**
- CDC and WHO provide separate growth charts for ages 2–19

---

## Important Limitations of BMI

BMI is a **screening tool**, not a diagnostic of body fatness or health:

1. **Does not distinguish muscle from fat** — athletes with high muscle mass may have elevated BMI despite low body fat
2. **Does not account for fat distribution** — waist circumference is often used as a complementary measure
3. **Does not reflect ethnicity, sex, or age differences** in body composition
4. **Not applicable** to pregnant women, those with certain medical conditions, or extreme body types

---

## Updated WHO Recommendations

Recent WHO guidance emphasizes that obesity diagnosis should **combine BMI with additional measurements** such as:
- **Waist circumference** (central adiposity indicator)
- **Body fat percentage**
- Population-specific adjustments

This addresses the limitation that traditional BMI alone can misclassify up to 30% of adults with "normal-weight obesity" (normal BMI but high body fat).

---

## Clinical and Surgical Applications

| Application | BMI Criteria |
|-------------|-------------|
| General weight-loss medication (e.g., Zepbound) | BMI ≥30, or BMI ≥27 with comorbidities |
| Bariatric surgery (standard) | BMI ≥35, or BMI 30–34.9 with metabolic disease |
| Bariatric surgery (Asian patients) | BMI >27.5 |
| NICE UK surgery guidelines | BMI ≥40, or BMI 35–39.9 with comorbidities |

---

Sources:
1. https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/9464-body-mass-index-bmi
2. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/losing-weight/bmi-in-adults
3. https://www.cdc.gov/bmi/adult-calculator/bmi-categories.html
4. https://www.uptodate.com/contents/image?imageKey=OBGYN%2F97661
5. https://apps.who.int/nutrition/landscape/help.aspx?menu=0&helpid=420
6. https://www.myheart.org.sg/tools-resources/bmi-calculator/
7. http://www.nhc.gov.cn/ylyjs/s3573d/202412/4cf1905d32304c15ac3bc4446ddb83f1/files/f932c5c0004f4959b92613dd1024483c.pdf
8. https://www.chinacdc.cn/jkkp/mxfcrb/lnjk/202408/t20240823_295135.html
9. https://bmicalculatorweb.com/blog/who-new-bmi-classification-obesity-diagnosis-criteria.html
10. https://carelyclinic.com/gastric-sleeve-eligibility-criteria/
